title: Entitlement Provenance and Retention Framework
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview:

This document defines Redwood Inference's Entitlement Provenance and Retention Framework (EPRF). It standardizes how we record, store, validate, and retrieve evidence that an entitlement (role, permission, attribute, or delegation) existed and was applied to a specific decision for the purposes of audits, incident response, and regulatory requests. The goal is to balance forensic fidelity, privacy/residency requirements, and operational cost.

Scope:

- System coverage: control plane (console/API), service control plane (service-to-service authorizers), identity lifecycle (SCIM, SSO, provisioning integrations), and privileged operations (admin consoles, automation runbooks).
- Evidence types included: entitlement assignments, authorization decision logs, role-change artifacts, approval records, delegation handoffs, JIT activations, and deprovisioning receipts.
- Not included: raw application payloads unrelated to access decisions (handled by product teams under data-retention policy).

Definitions:

- Entitlement: Any RBAC/ABAC construct granting a principal access to a resource.
- Provenance Record: A verifiable artifact that shows who changed an entitlement, when, why, and how it was approved.
- Evidence Package: A signed collection of provenance records, decision logs, and supporting artifacts produced for audits or incidents.

Principles:

1. Verifiability: Every evidence package must include cryptographic hashes for integrity and an audit trail linking elements to the originating service and operator.
2. Minimalism: Retain only data necessary for compliance and security investigations; apply redaction for PII where possible.
3. Region-aware retention: Residency and retention durations must respect customer and regulatory constraints.
4. Fast retrieval: On legal-hold or incident requests, evidence retrieval SLA is <= 24 hours for high-priority escalations, <= 72 hours for standard requests.
5. Cost-conscious archival: Less-frequently accessed evidence should move to cold immutable storage with clear rehydration steps.

Governance and Roles:

- Access Governance Board (AGB) – quarterly reviews, approves retention exceptions and classification mappings. Owner: Security, Chair: Director of Trust.
- Evidence Custodian – maintains storage, ingestion, and retrieval tooling. Owner: Eng-Platform.
- Entitlement Owner – service or team that defines a role and associated resources. Responsible for justification and audit responses.
- Incident Commander – triggers evidence collection on security incidents.

Evidence Catalog (summary table):

| Artifact Type | Source | Retention Tier | Retention Period | Provenance Fields | Storage Class | Retrieval SLA | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---|
| Authorization Decision Log | authz-proxy, OPA, service middleware | hot | 1 year (region-sensitive) | principal, resource, action, policy_id, decision_ts, request_id, request_hash | encrypted object store | 24h | 100% sampling for privileged APIs |
| Role Assignment Record | IAM, SCIM events | cold | 7 years (or per regulation) | assigned_by, approved_by, justification_id, ts | WORM object store | 72h | include approval tickets |
| JIT Activation Audit | just-in-time service | hot | 90 days | activator, duration, scope, approval_flow_id | encrypted object store | 24h | TTL enforced; snapshot to cold if escalated |
| Deprovision Receipt | deprovision pipeline | cold | 7 years | actor, effected_principal, assets_reconciled, ts | WORM | 72h | used for termination audits |
| Delegation Handoff | delegation service | cold | 5 years | delegator, delegatee, scope, expiry, evidence_hash | WORM | 72h | sign with delegation key |
| Approval Artifacts | Ticketing system (JIRA) export | cold | 7 years | ticket_id, approvers, timestamps, attachments_hash | archival store | 72h | attachments stored separately with hash references |

Retention & Residency Rules:

- EU customer-affiliated artifacts: stored in EU regions only. Retention windows may be shortened by Data Subject Request (DSR) claims unless a legal hold is in effect.
- US regulated customers (FINRA, HIPAA): retain as contractual commitments; follow the longer period if conflicts arise.
- Default retention baseline (unless contract or law requires otherwise): 1 year for hot authz logs, 7 years for entitlement provenance and approval artifacts.
- Cross-border replication: disabled by default for restricted artifacts; replication must be approved by AGB.

Evidence Provenance & Integrity Controls (procedures):

1. Ingestion: Services emit canonical JSON event for each entitlement change/decision with standardized schema (see example). Events MUST include request_id (UUIDv4), service_id, principal_id, and timestamp in RFC3339.

2. Hashing and signing: Ingestion pipeline computes SHA256 over canonical JSON and records a base64 signature using the service's signing key. A manifest with {request_id, sha256, signer_id, signed_ts} is stored alongside the artifact.

3. Linkage: Authorization decision logs must reference the entitlement assignment id when a role was used to authorize a decision. This creates a direct evidence graph for auditors.

4. Tamper-evidence: Store manifests in an append-only ledger (internal index) and replicate ledger checkpoints to an independent immutable store (WORM).

Example event (canonicalized JSON snippet):

{
  "request_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "service_id": "authz-proxy-eu-1",
  "principal_id": "svc:deploy-bot@redwood",
  "action": "deploy:create",
  "resource": "infra:cluster:eu-west-1:cluster-12",
  "decision": "ALLOW",
  "policy_id": "policy-iam-0143",
  "entitlement_assignment_id": "assign-2024-09-03-987",
  "ts": "2026-05-12T15:42:07Z"
}

(Above is for reference; production artifacts are stored as newline-delimited canonical JSON with accompanying manifest).

Audit & Retrieval Procedures (numbered playbook):

1. Request intake: Security or Legal opens Evidence Request ticket with classification (incident / audit / legal-hold) and priority.
2. Triage and scope: Evidence Custodian maps required artifact types, retention buckets, and regions. Identify PII redaction needs.
3. Preservation: For artifacts in hot storage, mark as preserved; for cold storage, ensure object is rehydrated and its manifest validated.
4. Assembly: Collect logs, manifests, approval artifacts, and compute an Evidence Package manifest with checksums and signer verification.
4a. If evidence crosses regions, record explicit justification; obtain AGB approval for cross-border movement when necessary.
5. Delivery: Deliver package via encrypted transfer (S3 pre-signed URL with IP restriction or secure courier for offline) to requestor. Log recipient and timestamp in chain-of-custody ledger.
6. Post-delivery: AGB reviews if any retention exceptions or follow-up action is required.

Exception Handling & Change Requests:

- Shorten-retention requests: Team must file a Change Request; AGB approves only when a lower retention does not breach contractual/regulatory commitments.
- Emergency legal-hold: Legal can override retention and rehydrate cold archives; Evidence Custodian must produce evidence within the 24h SLA for high-priority holds.

SDLC and CI/CD Integration:

- SDLC gating: Any change that affects entitlement assignment schema or ingestion pipeline must include a compliance checklist and integration tests verifying: manifest creation, signing, and ledger checkpointing.
- Release requirement: A rollout affecting authz decision flow requires a canary evaluation that validates 100% of privileged decision logging is intact for the canary cohort for at least 72 hours before full rollout.

Incident Response Tie-ins:

- On compromise suspicion (e.g., credential theft), Incident Commander triggers an immediate evidence snapshot: freeze logs for affected services and create a signed evidence bundle.
- For suspected exfiltration related to entitlement abuse, priority retrieval of delegation handoffs and role-assignment records is required.

Operational Metrics & SLOs:

- Evidence retrieval SLA (high priority): 24 hours, 95th percentile.
- Manifest verification success rate: 99.9% per month.
- Ledger checkpointing latency: < 5 minutes from ingestion, 99th percentile.
- Cross-region replication frequency (when enabled): daily, with explicit AGB approvals tracked.

Implementation Notes & Tooling:

- Use KMS/HSM-backed signing keys for service signatures; keys rotated on a schedule and archived in the key-rotation ledger.
- Manifests and ledger indices are stored in encrypted object storage with immutability flags set for retention periods.
- Provide a CLI (evidencectl) for teams to request, validate, and package evidence. Example commands:
  - evidencectl request --ticket JIRA-1234 --scope "service:authz-proxy:2026-05" --priority high
  - evidencectl validate --package /tmp/evidence-1234.tar.gz

Checklist for Owners (quick reference):

- Ensure service emits canonicalized entitlement events.
- Confirm manifests are signed and ledger checkpoints appear within 5 minutes.
- Tag artifacts with region and retention label on ingest.
- Register entitlement owners and maintain contact info for audit responses.

Appendix A — Retention Matrix (quick reference):

- Hot authz decisions: 1 year (hot) -> 3 years (cold) -> purge unless legal hold.
- Entitlement provenance (assign/approve): 7 years (WORM).
- Delegations/JIT: 5 years (WORM).
- Approval tickets & attachments: 7 years (encrypted archive).

Appendix B — Proof-of-Provenance Checklist for Evidence Packages:

- [ ] All artifacts have SHA256 computed and recorded in manifest.
- [ ] At least one signed checkpoint from ledger stored alongside package.
- [ ] Approver identities validated and cross-referenced to directory snapshot at time-of-change.
- [ ] Redaction applied where PII is outside requested scope.

Questions & Contact:

For governance or exception requests, contact Security (security@redwood.ai) or Evidence Custodian (evidence-custodian@redwood.ai). For tool issues, open an Eng-Platform ticket and tag AGB.
